mainTopic: The story of ושתי's downfall, the king's advisors and letters, and the meaning of מרדכי's names and tribe
overview: This amud opens with the last word of a saying from the previous amud. The גמרא then explains that the seventh day of אחשורוש's feast was שבת, when the nations' crude talk led to the demand that ושתי appear unclothed. That was a punishment measure for measure, because she had forced Jewish girls to work unclothed on שבת. The גמרא explains why ושתי refused (צרעת or a tail) and why the king was so furious (she sent him an insult). The Jewish חכמים wisely avoided judging her and sent him to the advisors of עמון and מואב. רבי לוי reads the advisors' names as hints to the קרבנות, and ממוכן is identified as המן. רבא shows how the king's silly first letters later saved the Jews, and רבי contrasts how דוד and אחשורוש each searched for a wife. Finally, the גמרא asks what the names in מרדכי's family line mean and why he is called both יהודי and ימיני. רבא's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the earlier proverb about husband and wife
steps.stepSummary: The last word of a proverb from the previous discussion, finishing the picture of husband and wife acting alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: …with zucchinis.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes a saying that began on the previous amud. That saying showed that a husband and wife often do similar things, just as אחשורוש and ושתי each made a party.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full proverb compares a man working with one kind of gourd and his wife with a similar kind. This word closes that comparison. Then the גמרא moves on to a new פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to read this word as the start of a new idea. It is just the tail end of a sentence from the previous section.

phrases.english: with zucchinis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the proverb earlier.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Husband and wife often do similar things, as אחשורוש and ושתי both made feasts.

steps.title: Why was the king merry only on the seventh day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק saying the king was merry with wine on the seventh day. It asks whether that means he was not merry during the first six days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'On the seventh day, when the king's heart was merry with wine.' Does that mean that until now he wasn't merry with wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a פסוק in מגילת אסתר and points out that its wording seems strange. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The party had been going on for days with plenty of wine. So saying he became merry 'on the seventh day' sounds as if the earlier days were sober. The question pushes us to find what was special about day seven.

keyTerms.meaning: when the heart was merry (from drinking)
is that to say…? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: "On the seventh day,
phrases.notes: אסתר 1:10

phrases.english: when the heart of the king was merry with wine."
Is that to say that until now
his heart was not merry with wine?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ עַד הַשְׁתָּא לָא טָב לִבֵּיהּ בְּחַמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion on the next פסוק in the מגילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'on the seventh day' in אסתר 1:10
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The king had been drinking all week, so naming the seventh day seems pointless unless something about that day was different.

steps.title: רבא: The seventh day was שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the seventh day was שבת. On שבת, Jews begin their meals with תורה and praise of ה׳, while the nations begin with crude talk. That is why the drunken crudeness showed up on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The seventh day was שבת. When Jews eat and drink, they begin with words of תורה and praise. But when the nations eat and drink, they begin only with crude, immoral talk.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by saying the seventh day was שבת. The contrast between how Jews and non-Jews celebrate explains the 'merriment' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'merry heart' is not ordinary drinking. It is the particular crude joy the nations show at a festive meal, which stood out on שבת, the day of feasting. This sets up the story in the next step, where the crude talk leads to the demand about ושתי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the whole explanation of ושתי's punishment, which is tied to שבת.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The seventh day was Shabbat.
For when Jews eat and drink,
they begin with words of Torah
and with words of praise.
But the nations of the world, when they eat and drink,
begin only with crude, immoral talk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא: יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שַׁבָּת הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the פסוק: the seventh day had special meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to say the king was sober for six days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seventh day was שבת, when the nations' crude kind of celebration showed most clearly.

steps.title: The crude conversation at אחשורוש's feast
steps.stepSummary: At אחשורוש's feast the men argued over whether Median or Persian women were more beautiful. אחשורוש offered to show them his Chaldean wife ושתי, and they demanded she appear unclothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too at the feast of that wicked man: some said Median women are beautiful, and others said Persian women are beautiful. אחשורוש said: The 'vessel' I use is neither Median nor Persian but Chaldean. Do you want to see her? They said: Yes, but only if she is unclothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows רבא's point in action: the feast's talk quickly turned crude. This leads straight to the order that ושתי appear before the guests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fills in what the פסוק leaves out, which is why the king called for ושתי at all. The crude 'beauty contest' talk is an example of the דברי תיפלות from step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the vessel I use,' a crude way of saying 'my wife'

phrases.english: And so too at the feast of that wicked man,
phrases.notes: "That wicked man" is אחשורוש.

phrases.english: some said: Median women are beautiful,
and others said: Persian women are beautiful.
Achashverosh said to them:
The vessel that I use,
phrases.notes: He crudely means his wife ושתי.

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ לֹא מָדִיִּי וְלֹא פָּרְסִי אֶלָּא כַּשְׂדִּיִּי,
phrases.english: is neither Median nor Persian, but Chaldean.
Do you wish to see her?
They said to him: Yes,
provided that she be unclothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete example of רבא's point about the nations' crude talk.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The feast's crude talk led to the demand that ושתי appear unclothed.

steps.title: Measure for measure: what ושתי had done
steps.stepSummary: The demand was a fitting punishment. ושתי had forced Jewish girls to be unclothed and to work on שבת, so she was punished in the same way, on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For with the measure a person uses to measure others, he is measured. This teaches that the wicked ושתי would bring Jewish girls, strip them unclothed, and make them work on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ושתי suffered this disgrace: it matched exactly what she had done to Jewish girls. The next step brings a פסוק to back this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects all the pieces. The day was שבת (step 3), and the demand was that she be unclothed (step 4). Both details mirror her own sin against בנות ישראל, which is the rule of מדה כנגד מדה.

keyTerms.term: בַּמִּדָּה שֶׁאָדָם מוֹדֵד בָּהּ מוֹדְדִין לוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: measure for measure: a person is treated the way he treats others

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the idea of מדה כנגד מדה running through the מגילה: ה׳ repays people in a way that matches what they did.

phrases.english: For with the measure that a person measures
with it he is measured,
this teaches that the wicked Vashti would
bring Jewish girls
and strip them unclothed
and make them do work on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁבַּמִּדָּה שֶׁאָדָם מוֹדֵד בָּהּ מוֹדְדִין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the disgrace described in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ושתי was shamed unclothed on שבת because she had shamed Jewish girls unclothed on שבת.

steps.title: Proof from the verse: 'what she did and what was decreed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the idea with אסתר 2:1. The פסוק places 'what she had done' next to 'what was decreed upon her,' which shows the punishment matched the sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what is written: 'After these things, when King אחשורוש's anger calmed, he remembered ושתי, and what she had done, and what was decreed upon her.' Just as she did, so was decreed upon her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that proves ושתי's punishment matched her actions. This closes the measure-for-measure point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'what she did' and 'what was decreed' side by side. The גמרא reads this as saying the decree was a mirror image of her deeds. That is the source for the מדה כנגד מדה idea in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what is written (the פסוק supports this)

steps.whatToRemember: The seventh day was שבת. The crude feast talk led to the demand that ושתי appear unclothed, and this matched exactly what she had done to Jewish girls on שבת: מדה כנגד מדה.

phrases.english: This is what is written:
"After these things,
phrases.notes: This is אסתר 2:1, after ושתי was removed as queen.

phrases.english: when the anger of King Achashverosh calmed down,

phrases.aramaic: זָכַר אֶת וַשְׁתִּי וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂתָה
phrases.english: he remembered Vashti and what she had done
and what was decreed upon her."
Just as she had done, so it was decreed upon her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק to support the measure-for-measure claim of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That ושתי's punishment matched her own sin
steps.raayaSupportSource: אסתר 2:1, which places 'what she had done' next to 'what was decreed upon her'

steps.title: Why would an immodest queen refuse to come?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'ושתי refused' and asks why. We were taught she had the same sinful intentions as אחשורוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says Queen ושתי refused. But she was immodest, since we learned that both of them intended sin. So why did she not come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the next פסוק and points out that it seems to contradict something we already know about ושתי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that ושתי was just as immodest as אחשורוש. A woman like that should have been happy to show off. So her refusal needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all (opens a question built on known facts)

phrases.english: "But Queen Vashti refused" (Esther 1:12).
Since she was an immodest woman,
as the Master said:
The two of them intended a sinful matter,
phrases.notes: "The two of them" means אחשורוש and ושתי.

phrases.english: what is the reason she did not come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק in the story and questions the queen's behavior.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An immodest woman who shared the king's intentions would not be expected to refuse.

steps.title: She broke out in צרעת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers that ושתי suddenly broke out in צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: This teaches that צרעת broke out on her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers the question. ושתי wanted to come but could not, because her skin broke out in צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The refusal was not modesty. Something happened to her body that made her ashamed to show herself, so the question falls away.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
This teaches that leprosy broke out on her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New fact added to the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think ושתי refused out of modesty or pride.
steps.terutzMaskana: She refused because צרעת made her ashamed to appear.

steps.title: גבריאל gave her a tail
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a different answer: the angel גבריאל came and made ושתי grow a tail.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: גבריאל came and made her a tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer to the same question, this time from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is the same as before: something embarrassing happened to her body, so she could not appear. Only the cause is different, an angel making her a tail instead of צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Gabriel came and made her a tail.
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets; they're part of the corrected wording, so read them as part of the line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of step 7.
steps.terutzMaskana: A miraculous tail embarrassed her and kept her away.

steps.title: Why was the king so furious?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the king became very angry. The גמרא asks why one refusal made him burn with so much rage.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the king was very angry.' Why did his anger burn in him so much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the next words of the פסוק and asks why his anger was so extreme.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A refusal alone seems too small to cause such strong anger. The word 'very' and the phrase 'his anger burned in him' suggest something more happened.

keyTerms.meaning: So much, to such a degree

phrases.english: "And the king was very angry" (Esther 1:12).
Why did it burn in him so much?
phrases.notes: "It" means his anger. The פסוק goes on to say "his anger burned in him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the king's reaction to her refusal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The strength of the king's anger in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simple refusal does not seem to justify such burning rage.

steps.title: ושתי's insulting message
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ושתי sent an insult. She called אחשורוש her father's stable boy and said he couldn't hold his wine like her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: She sent him a message: 'Son of my father's stableman! My father drank wine in front of a thousand men and did not get drunk, and that man has become foolish from his wine.' Right away, 'his anger burned in him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that ושתי did more than refuse. She sent back a humiliating insult, and that is what set off the king's fury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her message attacked him twice. It mocked his low birth, as a servant in her royal family's stables, and his weakness with wine compared to her father בלשאצר. That explains why the פסוק says his anger 'burned' right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Stableman, groom who cares for horses

phrases.english: Rava said: She sent him a message:
Son of my father's stableman!
My father drank wine in front of a thousand
phrases.notes: Her father is בלשאצר. דניאל 5:1 says he drank wine before a thousand of his lords.

phrases.english: and did not get drunk,
and that man has become foolish from his wine.
phrases.notes: "That man" is a polite way of saying "you." She means אחשורוש himself.

phrases.english: Immediately: "and his anger burned in him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New fact added to the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed he was this furious over a simple refusal.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was furious because she sent a deeply insulting message.

steps.title: Who were the wise men?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the king spoke to the wise men, and the גמרא asks who they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the king said to the wise men.' Who are these wise men?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next point by asking whom the פסוק means when it says 'the wise men.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a plain question to identify people in the פסוק, not an attack. The answer in the next step will drive the rest of the story.

phrases.english: "And the king said to the wise men" (Esther 1:13),
who are the wise men?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק, where the angry king seeks advice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the 'wise men' in the פסוק

steps.title: The wise men were the Jewish רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The wise men were the רבנן. They are called 'those who know the times' because they knew how to set the Jewish calendar.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were the Rabbis. 'Who know the times' means they know how to add a month to years and how to fix the months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the 'wise men' were the Jewish חכמים. It proves this from the next words of the פסוק, 'who know the times.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing 'the times' is read as knowing the Jewish calendar: adding a month to make a leap year and fixing when each month starts. That skill belongs to the Jewish חכמים, so the פסוק must mean them.

keyTerms.meaning: To add a month and make a leap year
To fix when the months begin

phrases.english: The Rabbis.
"Who know the times"
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: for they know how to make leap years
phrases.notes: Literally "to make years pregnant," meaning to add an extra month to the year.

phrases.english: and how to fix the months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wise men were the Jewish חכמים, who set the calendar.

steps.title: The חכמים' dangerous dilemma
steps.stepSummary: אחשורוש asks the חכמים to judge ושתי. They see that either ruling would get them in trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Judge her for me. They said: What should we do? If we tell him to kill her, tomorrow he will be sober and demand her back from us. If we tell him to let her go, she has disgraced the kingdom.
steps.whatsHappening: The king asks the Jewish חכמים to judge ושתי. They think it through and see that any verdict is a trap. This sets up their clever reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A death sentence is risky because the king might regret it once sober and blame them. Letting her go is risky because it ignores an insult to the throne. Since both options are dangerous, they need a way out.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave her alone, let her be

phrases.english: He said to them: Judge her for me.
They said: What should we do?
If we tell him: Kill her,
tomorrow his wine will wear off
and he will demand her from us.
If we tell him: Let her be,
she is disgracing the kingdom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the wise men are identified, the story shows what the king asked them and how they weighed it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any verdict on ושתי would put the חכמים in danger.

steps.title: The חכמים politely decline
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell the king that since the חורבן they can no longer judge דיני נפשות. They send him to the settled nations of עמון and מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed and we were exiled from our land, good judgment has been taken from us, and we do not know how to judge capital cases. Go to עמון and מואב, who have stayed settled in their places like wine resting on its lees.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים escape their trap. They say exile has weakened their judgment, and they send the king to advisors from nations that were never exiled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their excuse is respectful and safe. They don't refuse the king outright; they say they are not qualified. The image of wine resting on its lees means a people who stayed in one place kept their minds clear and steady.

keyTerms.meaning: Good counsel and judgment were taken from us
Capital cases, cases of life and death
Lees, the sediment wine rests on

phrases.english: They said to him:
From the day that the Temple was destroyed
and we were exiled from our land,
counsel has been taken from us

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִין לָדוּן דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת.
phrases.english: and we do not know how to judge capital cases.
Go to Ammon and Moab,
who stay settled in their places
like wine that rests on its lees.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְגָלִינוּ מֵאַרְצֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the way out the חכמים chose after weighing their dilemma.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים avoided judging by saying exile had taken away their judgment, and sent the king to עמון and מואב.

steps.title: A פסוק backs their advice, and the king follows it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the חכמים' reason was a good one and proves it from a פסוק in ירמיהו about מואב. Then the king immediately turns to his own advisors.
steps.simpleTranslation: They gave him a good reason, as it is written: 'מואב has been at ease from his youth, he has settled on his lees, he has not been poured from vessel to vessel, and he has not gone into exile. Therefore his taste has stayed in him and his scent has not changed.' Right away: 'And next to him were כרשנא, שתר, אדמתא, תרשיש.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the חכמים' wine comparison comes straight from a פסוק. Then it shows the king taking their advice at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו 48:11 describes מואב as wine never poured out or moved into exile, so its 'taste' stayed. The word טעמא means 'reason,' and the פסוק speaks of מואב's 'taste' (טעמו), so the advice fits its proof. The king's quick turn to his own advisors, named in אסתר 1:14, shows he accepted it.

keyTerms.meaning: And a (good) reason; also related to 'taste'

steps.whatToRemember: ושתי refused because of a sudden bodily shame (צרעת or a tail). The king raged because she insulted him. The Jewish חכמים wisely avoided judging her by sending him to the advisors of the settled nations.

phrases.english: And they gave him a good reason,
as it is written:
"Moab has been at ease from his youth,
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from ירמיהו 48:11.

phrases.english: and he has settled on his lees,
and he has not been emptied from vessel to vessel,
and he has not gone into exile;
therefore his taste has remained in him,
and his scent has not changed."
Immediately:
"And next to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish" (Esther 1:14).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the wine comparison of step 15 with a פסוק and closes the episode.
steps.raayaObject: The חכמים' claim that a nation never exiled keeps its clear judgment, like settled wine
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 48:11, about מואב resting on its lees and never going into exile

steps.title: The advisors' names hint at the offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי says that the whole פסוק listing the king's advisors (אסתר א:יד) is really about קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: this whole פסוק was said because of the קרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי makes a new claim: the list of the king's seven advisors in the מגילה is secretly talking about קרבנות. This sets up the next step, where each name is explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, the פסוק is only a list of Persian names. רבי לוי says there is a hidden layer: each name hints at a different part of the עבודה in the בית המקדש. The next step shows how each name works.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings brought in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
This entire verse
was said on account of offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: כׇּל פָּסוּק זֶה עַל שׁוּם קׇרְבָּנוֹת נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 16 ended with the king turning to his own advisors. רבי לוי now explains the hidden meaning of those advisors' names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The list of advisors' names hints at the קרבנות.

steps.title: The angels plead using each advisor's name
steps.stepSummary: Each name is read as a hint to a different part of the עבודה. The מלאכי השרת use these hints to ask הקב״ה: did the other nations ever serve You like the Jews did?
steps.simpleTranslation: כרשנא: the angels said to הקב״ה, did the nations ever offer You year-old lambs the way the Jews did? שתר: did they ever offer two turtledoves? אדמתא: did they ever build You an altar of earth? תרשיש: did they ever serve You in the priestly clothes, which have the תרשיש stone? מרס: did they ever stir the blood for You? מרסנא: did they ever stir the מנחות for You? ממוכן: did they ever prepare the שולחן for You?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the seven names one by one. It shows how each name sounds like a word connected to the עבודה in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is broken into a sound-alike: כרשנא is כרים בני שנה, שתר is שתי תורין, and so on. The angels are speaking up for the Jews: at a moment of danger, they remind הקב״ה that only Israel served Him this way.

keyTerms.meaning: The special clothes worn by the כהנים
They stirred (to keep blood from clotting or to mix flour)
The table in the מקדש that held the לחם הפנים

steps.confusionAlert: These are not real meanings of the Persian names. The גמרא is reading hints into the sounds of the names, a typical אגדה style.

phrases.english: "Carshena" —
phrases.notes: כר (lamb) plus שנה (year) gives "year-old lamb."

phrases.english: the ministering angels said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
did they ever offer before You
phrases.notes: "They" means the other nations, as opposed to the Jews.

phrases.english: lambs in their first year
the way the Jewish people offered before You?
"Shethar" — did they ever offer before You
two turtledoves?
phrases.notes: שתר sounds like שתי תור, "two turtledoves."

phrases.english: "Admatha" — did they ever build before You
an altar of earth?
"Tarshish" — did they ever serve before You
in the priestly garments,
about which it is written
"A beryl, an onyx, and a jasper"?
phrases.notes: These are stones on the כהן גדול's breastplate, so the name תרשיש points to the priestly clothes.

phrases.english: "Meres" — did they ever stir the blood before You?
"Marsena" — did they ever stir the meal-offerings before You?
"Memucan" — did they ever prepare the table before You?
phrases.notes: ממוכן sounds like מוכן, "prepared."

steps.triggerLanguage: ״כַּרְשְׁנָא״ — אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out רבי לוי's claim from step 17, name by name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the seven names hints at a unique part of Israel's עבודה, which the angels mention in Israel's favor.

steps.title: ממוכן was really המן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that ממוכן, the advisor who spoke up against ושתי, was המן. He is called ממוכן because he was ready for disaster.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "And ממוכן said." A ברייתא taught: ממוכן is המן. Why is he called ממוכן? Because he was prepared for disaster.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק, where ממוכן gives the king advice. It brings a ברייתא that identifies ממוכן as המן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name ממוכן is read as מוכן, "prepared." המן was "prepared for פורענות": he was ready to bring calamity on the Jews, or calamity was ready to come upon him.

phrases.english: "And Memucan said."
phrases.notes: This is אסתר א:טז, where ממוכן advises the king to punish ושתי.

phrases.english: It was taught: Memucan is Haman.
And why is he called Memucan?
Because he was prepared for calamity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the list of names to the next פסוק, where ממוכן actually speaks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ממוכן is המן, so called because he was ready for calamity.

steps.title: The lowly person jumps ahead
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא learns from ממוכן speaking first that a common, lowly person pushes himself to the front.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: from here we learn that the common person jumps to the front.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא draws a life lesson from the פסוק. ממוכן was listed last of the seven advisors, yet he was the first to speak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the list ממוכן comes seventh, which shows he was the least important. Still, when the king asked, he answered first. רב כהנא sees this as typical: the lowly person rushes to speak before his betters.

keyTerms.meaning: Jumps to the front / pushes ahead first

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
From here we see that the common man jumps to the front.
phrases.notes: ממוכן was named last of the seven, but he spoke up before everyone else.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: מִכָּאן שֶׁהַהֶדְיוֹט קוֹפֵץ בָּרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק ("ויאמר ממוכן") together with the order of names from step 18 to teach a lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lowly person rushes to put himself first.

steps.title: The silly first letters saved the Jews
steps.stepSummary: The king's first letters said every man should rule in his own house. רבא says that without these letters, the Jews would have been wiped out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "That every man should rule in his own house." רבא said: if not for the first letters, not one survivor would have been left of the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the king's decree after ושתי was removed. רבא says this odd decree is what later saved the Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone laughed at the first letters, since obviously a man rules in his own house. So people stopped taking the king's letters seriously. When המן's later letters ordered the Jews killed, people did not rush to act on them, and this gave time for the rescue.
steps.whatToRemember: Even the king's foolish decree about ושתי was part of the hidden plan: it made people doubt his later letters, and that helped save the Jews.
steps.confusionAlert: "The enemies of Israel" here means Israel itself. The גמרא avoids saying something bad directly about the Jews.
steps.whyThisMatters: This fits the big theme of the מגילה: הקב״ה sets up the cure before the disaster, even through events that look random.

phrases.english: "That every man shall rule in his own house."
phrases.notes: This is from the king's letters after ושתי was punished (אסתר א:כב).

phrases.english: Rava said:
Were it not for the first letters,
there would not have remained of the enemies of Israel
phrases.notes: This is a polite way of saying "of Israel." חז״ל avoid saying something bad about the Jews directly.

phrases.english: a survivor or an escapee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves forward in the story to the result of ממוכן's advice: the king sends out letters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ridiculous first letters made people doubt the king, which saved the Jews from the later decree.

steps.title: Why people laughed at the king's first letters
steps.stepSummary: The people who got the first letters mocked them. Of course every man is boss in his own house, so why send a royal order about it?
steps.simpleTranslation: People said: Why did he send us a letter saying 'every man should rule in his own house'? That is obvious! Even a simple weaver is the boss in his own home!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the people did not take the king's first letters seriously. It also shows why רבא's point in the last step makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 21, רבא said the first letters saved the Jews. This step shows how: the letters made the king look foolish. People thought his order was silly, so later they did not rush to obey his letters at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A commander, an officer in charge

steps.whatToRemember: The first letters ended up protecting the Jews because they made the king look foolish. People learned not to take his letters seriously, so they did not rush to carry out the later decree.

phrases.english: They would say: What is this that he sent us:
phrases.notes: "They" means the people in the provinces who got the king's first letters.

phrases.english: "That every man shall rule in his own house"?
phrases.notes: This is quoted from אסתר א:כב, the king's order after ושתי refused to come.

phrases.english: That is obvious! Even a lowly weaver
is the commander in his own house!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the first letters ended up saving the Jews, as רבא said in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first letters made the king look foolish, so people stopped taking his letters seriously.

steps.title: Asking about a פסוק in משלי while discussing the king's officers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about אחשורוש appointing officers to gather the young women. Then רבי asks what the פסוק 'a wise man acts with knowledge, but a fool spreads out his foolishness' is coming to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And let the king appoint officers." רבי said: What does this פסוק mean: "Every wise man acts with knowledge, but a fool spreads out his foolishness"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new פסוק in the מגילה, the search for a new queen. רבי asks about a פסוק in משלי, and this question sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'מאי דכתיב' is a common way to open a teaching about a פסוק. רבי is about to show that the משלי פסוק is talking about two kings who each looked for a wife.

phrases.english: "And let the king appoint officers."
phrases.notes: אסתר ב:ג

phrases.english: Rabbi said: What is the meaning of what is written:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: "Every wise man acts with knowledge,
phrases.notes: משלי יג:טז

phrases.english: but a fool spreads out his foolishness"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the first letters to the next event in the מגילה, the search for a new queen.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the משלי פסוק about the wise man and the fool is talking about.

steps.title: דוד searched wisely and אחשורוש searched foolishly
steps.stepSummary: The wise man in the פסוק is דוד, who asked for one young woman, so every father brought his daughter. The fool is אחשורוש, who appointed officers to gather many young women, so every father hid his daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Every wise man acts with knowledge": this is דוד, as it says, "His servants said to him: Let them look for a young maiden for my master the king." Everyone who had a daughter brought her to him. "But a fool spreads out his foolishness": this is אחשורוש, as it says, "And let the king appoint officers." Everyone who had a daughter hid her from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers his own question. Each half of the משלי פסוק matches a different king's way of looking for a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד looked for one wife, so families wanted their daughters chosen. אחשורוש sent officers to gather many women, and only one would become queen. So families tried to hide their daughters, and his foolishness was 'spread out' for everyone to see.
steps.whatToRemember: The same goal, finding a wife for the king, can be done wisely or foolishly. With דוד, families brought their daughters. With אחשורוש, families hid them.

phrases.english: "Every wise man acts with knowledge": this is David,
as it is written: "And his servants said to him:
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from מלכים א א:ב, at the end of דוד's life.

phrases.english: Let them look for a young maiden for my master the king."

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מַאן דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ בְּרַתָּא — אַיָּיתַהּ נִיהֲלֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Anyone who had a daughter brought her to him.
"But a fool spreads out his foolishness": this is Achashverosh,
as it is written: "And let the king appoint officers";

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מַאן דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ בְּרַתָּא — אַיטְמְרַהּ מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Anyone who had a daughter hid her from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 23 about the meaning of the משלי פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wise man is דוד, and fathers brought their daughters to him. The fool is אחשורוש, and fathers hid their daughters from him.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק list only some of מרדכי's ancestors?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק introducing מרדכי names his father, grandfather and great-grandfather, then calls him 'a man of בנימין'. The גמרא asks: if the goal is to give his family line, why not trace it all the way back to בנימין? So what is special about these names?
steps.simpleTranslation: "There was a Jewish man in שושן הבירה … a man of בנימין." What is the פסוק telling us? If it wants to give his family line, it should trace him all the way back to בנימין! So what is special about these particular names?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the פסוק that introduces מרדכי. It asks a question that sets up the explanations in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is built in two parts. First: if the names are only there to show his family line, the list should go back to בנימין, the head of the tribe. Since it stops after three names, these names must be there for a reason. The גמרא will now explain what each name hints to.

keyTerms.meaning: A man from the tribe of בנימין
What is different? What is special?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying מרדכי's family line is unimportant. It is asking why the פסוק picked these few names in particular, which means each name probably hints to something.

phrases.english: "There was a Jewish man in Shushan the capital,
phrases.notes: This is from אסתר ב:ה, where מרדכי first appears.

phrases.english: etc. … a man of Benjamin."
phrases.notes: "Etc." skips the middle of the פסוק, which names his father יאיר, grandfather שמעי and great-grandfather קיש.

phrases.english: What is it saying?
If it comes to give his family line,
let it trace his line and keep going up to Benjamin!
Rather, what is special about these names?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the פסוק that introduces מרדכי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק names only מרדכי's father, grandfather and great-grandfather instead of his full family line back to בנימין.

steps.title: The ancestor names are really praises of מרדכי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that בן יאיר, בן שמעי and בן קיש are all names for מרדכי himself, each one praising his prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: all of these are names that מרדכי himself was called. 'Son of יאיר' means the son who lit up the eyes of the Jewish people with his prayer. 'Son of שמעי' means the son whose prayer God heard. 'Son of קיש' means he knocked on the gates of mercy and they were opened for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 25. The names in the פסוק are not just a family tree. They are nicknames that describe מרדכי himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 asked why the פסוק lists only three ancestors and does not trace the line all the way back to בנימין. The answer is that the three names are not mainly there for family history. Each name hints at a Hebrew word that describes מרדכי's powerful prayer: יאיר sounds like 'lit up', שמעי sounds like 'heard', and קיש sounds like 'knocked'.

keyTerms.meaning: They were called by his name. Here it means these are names for מרדכי himself.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'son of יאיר' as only meaning that his father was named יאיר. In this ברייתא, each 'son of' name is a description of מרדכי's own greatness.

phrases.english: It was taught: all of them are names he was called by.
phrases.notes: 'He' is מרדכי. All three names in the פסוק describe him personally.

phrases.english: 'Son of Jair' means a son who lit up
the eyes of the Jewish people with his prayer.
'Son of Shimei' means a son whose prayer God heard.
phrases.notes: Here אֵל means God. It does not mean 'to'.

phrases.english: 'Son of Kish' means that he knocked on the gates of mercy
and they were opened for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The names are not a full family tree. They are descriptive names that praise מרדכי's prayer.

steps.title: Is מרדכי from יהודה or from בנימין?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls מרדכי both יהודי, which suggests the tribe of יהודה, and ימיני, which means the tribe of בנימין. These seem to contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק calls him a 'יהודי', so it seems he comes from יהודה. But it also calls him a 'ימיני', so it seems he comes from בנימין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction inside the same פסוק about which tribe מרדכי came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'איש יהודי' and later 'איש ימיני'. If יהודי means 'from the tribe of יהודה', it clashes with ימיני, which clearly means 'from the tribe of בנימין'. A person cannot come from two tribes through his father, so the גמרא needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jew, or someone from the tribe of יהודה
Someone from the tribe of בנימין

phrases.english: It calls him 'Yehudi',
phrases.notes: This is אסתר 2:5: 'There was a Jewish man in שושן... a man of בנימין.'

phrases.english: which shows he comes from Judah;
and it calls him 'Yemini',
which shows he comes from Benjamin!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי לֵיהּ יְהוּדִי אַלְמָא מִיהוּדָה קָאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new difficulty from the same פסוק about מרדכי
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק's two descriptions of מרדכי, יהודי and ימיני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One name points to the tribe of יהודה and the other to the tribe of בנימין, so they seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: רב נחמן: יהודי is an honorary title
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that יהודי is a title of honor for מרדכי. It is not the name of his tribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: מרדכי was crowned with honorary names.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the first answer to the contradiction. יהודי is an honor title, while ימיני tells us his real tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this answer, only ימיני describes his tribe. יהודי is a crown-like name, connected to the royal tribe of יהודה, given to him because of his greatness. With that, the contradiction disappears.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Mordechai was crowned with his title.
phrases.notes: He means יהודי is a title of honor. It is not telling us his tribe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מָרְדֳּכַי מוּכְתָּר בְּנִימוּסוֹ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets one of the two terms
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהודי means he is from the tribe of יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: יהודי is an honorary title, and ימיני is his actual tribe.

steps.title: Father from בנימין, mother from יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers that both names are true: מרדכי's father was from בנימין and his mother was from יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: his father was from בנימין, and his mother was from יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the contradiction. Each name describes a different parent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב נחמן, this answer keeps יהודי as a real family connection. ימיני comes from his father's side and יהודי from his mother's side, so both names describe his actual family.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
His father was from Benjamin, and his mother was from Judah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two names between his two parents
steps.terutzMaskana: ימיני comes from his father and יהודי comes from his mother.

steps.title: The two tribes argue over who gets credit for מרדכי
steps.stepSummary: רבנן say both tribes claimed מרדכי. יהודה said its king דוד made his birth possible, and בנימין said he actually came from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say: the families argued with each other. The family of יהודה said: 'I caused מרדכי to be born, because דוד did not kill שמעי בן גרא.' The family of בנימין said: 'He comes from me.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer. Each name reflects a different tribe's claim on מרדכי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here מרדכי is fully from בנימין, but יהודה also claims some credit. דוד, from יהודה, chose not to kill שמעי בן גרא when שמעי cursed him. Since מרדכי later descended from שמעי, he could only be born because of דוד's choice. So the name יהודי reflects יהודה's credit, and ימיני reflects his actual tribe.

keyTerms.meaning: The man from בנימין who cursed דוד. מרדכי descended from him.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
The families competed with each other.
The family of Judah says:
I caused Mordechai to be born,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא קַטְלֵיהּ דָּוִד לְשִׁמְעִי בֶּן גֵּרָא.
phrases.english: since David did not kill Shimei son of Gera.
phrases.notes: שמעי cursed דוד while דוד was running from אבשלום, but דוד let him live. מרדכי later came from his family.

phrases.english: And the family of Benjamin said: He comes from me.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: מִשְׁפָּחוֹת מִתְגָּרוֹת זוֹ בָּזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the contradiction from step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each name reflects a different tribe's claim
steps.terutzMaskana: מרדכי is really from בנימין, but יהודה claims credit because דוד spared שמעי.

steps.title: רבא: the names are a complaint, not a boast
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the two names the opposite way: כנסת ישראל complains about what someone from יהודה did to it and how someone from בנימין paid it back. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: כנסת ישראל said it the other way around: 'See what a יהודי did to me, and how a ימיני paid me back.' What a יהודי did to me is...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a fourth approach, and this step sets up the next passage. He begins to explain 'what a יהודי did to me', and the explanation continues there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רבנן's answer, the tribes compete to take credit for מרדכי. רבא flips this around: the names are a complaint by the Jewish people, who say they suffered because of a person from יהודה and a person from בנימין. The details of each complaint come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jewish people as a whole
From the other side, the opposite way

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'paid me back' is said as a complaint, not as thanks. כנסת ישראל is blaming, not praising.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The Jewish people said it the opposite way:
See what a Judean did to me
and how a Benjamite paid me back.
What a Judean did to me —
